message.content: accord fixed-context probe. In one message, dispatch each of these subagent types once, with the description "fixed probe accord-executor" and the prompt "accord fixed-context probe: reply ok, use no tool": accord-executor. Use no other tool, then reply ok.

addedLines: - accord-architect: Reads the ticket and the code, runs an impact analysis, and proposes two or three options with the lightest that works first, for the approach stage. Never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- accord-auditor: Reads only the ticket and tries to find two different readings of each acceptance criterion, for the intent interview's audit. Never proposes fixes, never reads code. (Tools: Read)

- accord-critic: Argues the strongest case against a chosen approach or a plan, in a fresh context, checked against the ticket's Vetoes, Decisions, and Corrections. Never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- accord-debugger: Finds the root cause of a failure with competing hypotheses, ranked before any is tested, and records the investigation in debug.md, for the debug stage. Never fixes anything. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write)

- accord-executor: Builds the one plan task or fixes the review or debug findings its brief names, failing test first, and reports in at most 15 lines. Never edits the ticket or plan.md. (Tools: All tools)

- accord-final-reviewer: Reviews built work through one lens, intent, quality, security, integration, or both, against the ticket, the review package, and the ledger, and reports numbered findings each with a concrete failing case. Never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- accord-planner: Writes a ticket's plan.md, one task per section with covers, files, and verify lines, ordered wiring first and polish last, for the plan stage. Writes nothing else. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit)

- accord-reviewer: Reviews built work through one lens, intent, quality, security, integration, or both, against the ticket, the review package, and the ledger, and reports numbered findings each with a concrete failing case. Never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- accord-scout: Reads the code and returns facts with file and line, for the intent interview and the approach's impact analysis. Never proposes, never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- accord-verifier: Verifies built work against each acceptance criterion of the ticket at four levels, exists, substantive, wired, and data flows, and writes verification.md. Never edits anything else. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-security:claude-security: The Claude Security orchestrator, for use only as the main agent of a session (claude --agent claude-security:claude-security), where it runs a scan end to end and can turn its findings into targeted patch files, each verified by a panel of agents. Never dispatch it as a subagent: it cannot scan from there. When a user asks for Claude Security in a conversation, use the claude-security:claude-security skill instead. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion, Workflow, Workflow(claude-security:scan), TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent(claude-security:scan-inventory, claude-security:scan-researcher, claude-security:scan-verifier, claude-security:scan-loader, claude-security:scan-redactor, claude-security:patch-generator, claude-security:patch-verifier, claude-security:explore))

attachment.content:
- amazon-bedrock: Builds generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore (including the Harness managed agent loop). Applies when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, migrating/porting/converting a Bedrock Agent (including inline agents) to an AgentCore Harness, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing Bedrock models (Claude, Llama, Nova, Titan). Also for prompt caching, quota and throttling diagnosis, cost tracking, migrating between Claude model generations, chunking strategies, and Bedrock model selection. Covers AgentCore Payments (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, paid endpoints, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend. For SageMaker model discovery, customization, or endpoints, use aws-ai-ml.
- aws-ai-ml: Selects, deploys, and customizes AI models on Amazon SageMaker. Fine-tuning (SFT, DPO, RLVR, RLAIF), model selection, dataset preparation, evaluation, deployment to SageMaker endpoints or Bedrock, inference optimization and endpoint diagnostics. Covers the full lifecycle from planning through production. Use when fine-tuning models on SageMaker, choosing which base model to customize or fine-tune from SageMaker JumpStart or Hub, finding a model to deploy without fine-tuning, transforming datasets for training, checking data readiness, evaluating model quality, deploying to endpoints, benchmarking or optimizing inference, setting up IAM roles and S3 buckets for training jobs, or managing a SageMaker Managed MLflow app. Also use to check endpoint health, diagnose failures, debug latency or errors, or view container logs and CloudWatch metrics. Covers Serverless Model Customization, Nova and OSS deployment, and PySDK v3. NOT for Ground Truth labeling, Feature Store, or general-purpose AWS infrastructure.
- accord: Use when starting any work in an accord repository, when seeing where work stands, or when continuing a ticket. Shows the dashboard, continues or picks up a ticket, and classifies a new request into a lane.
- accord-approach: Use when a lane M ticket has its intent and acceptance criteria and needs an approach. Chooses the lightest approach that works, has a critic argue against it, and takes the owner's explicit yes before accord approve.
- accord-build: Use when a lane M ticket has a plan that passed accord gate plan and needs building. Dispatches one fresh executor per task from accord brief, runs the affected tests itself, and records each task with accord task-done.
- accord-debug: Use when a lane M ticket's work behaves unexpectedly, a test fails for a reason nobody has shown, or a fix did not work. Finds the root cause with a debugger before any fix, fixes it once through a fresh executor test first, and keeps its state in debug.md.
- accord-intent: Use when a lane M ticket needs its intent captured, or when /accord routes a new request here. Runs the intent interview that writes the ticket's Intent, acceptance criteria, Vetoes, Decisions, and Corrections, so later stages cannot drift from what the owner meant.
- accord-plan: Use when a lane M ticket has an approved approach and needs a plan. Has the planner write plan.md task by task, checks it with accord gate plan and the critic, and runs the full test suite on the baseline before build.
- accord-review: Use when every task of a lane M ticket has a ledger line and the work needs review. Dispatches reviewers on the review package, fixes patch findings through fresh executors until no Must is open and every Should is fixed, runs one final reviewer, and records each round in review.md.
- accord-verify: Use when a lane M ticket's review.md ends with a verdict and the work needs verifying. Runs the full suite, has a fresh verifier write verification.md, builds the owner's report, and runs accord gate done once the owner has approved verified.
